children: rose 0.30% premarket after Reuters reported it is weighing the sale of a majority stake in its Japan business at a valuation of about $3 billion, citing two people with knowledge of the matter. Starbucks has asked several financial advisers for pitches and is open to selling a majority stake. The stake size and final valuation remain undetermined.

Starbucks bought out its long-time partner Sazaby League in 2014 for roughly $914 million, taking full control at a valuation near $1.5 billion. The store count has grown from around 1,050 then to 1,883 as of September 2025, nearly 9% of the global footprint. International comparable sales rose 5.7% in the third quarter with Japan credited as a key driver.

Starbucks did something similar in China last year, ceding control of that business to Boyu Capital last year at a $4 billion valuation, closing in April, and said the total value including its retained stake and licensing income over at least ten years would exceed $13 billion.

title: Starbucks Could Sell Japan Control at a $3 Billion Valuation
